{"id":"PKIX-j32w.1","title":"Create pkix-dane crate (no_std DANE primitives)","description":"## What

New workspace crate `pkix-dane`. no_std-friendly. Provides:

- TLSA record types: usage (CertUsage), selector (Selector), matching type (MatchingType), association data
- DER / wire-format parsing for TLSA records
- Per-usage match logic per RFC 6698 §2.1 + RFC 7218 disambiguation:
  - usage 0 (PKIX-TA): constrain which CA must sign
  - usage 1 (PKIX-EE): constrain leaf cert
  - usage 2 (DANE-TA): synthesize trust anchor from TLSA-asserted cert/SPKI
  - usage 3 (DANE-EE): direct match on leaf cert, bypassing chain
- Per-usage verify functions:
  - `verify_pkix_ta(path: &ValidatedPath, tlsa: &[TlsaRecord]) -> Result<(), DaneError>`
  - `verify_pkix_ee(leaf: &Certificate, tlsa: &[TlsaRecord]) -> Result<(), DaneError>`
  - `verify_dane_ta(leaf: &Certificate, tlsa: &[TlsaRecord]) -> Result<TrustAnchor, DaneError>`
  - `verify_dane_ee(leaf: &Certificate, tlsa: &[TlsaRecord]) -> Result<(), DaneError>`
- DaneError enum — Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq + non_exhaustive, Send + Sync (per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6)
- No DNS. Caller supplies validated TLSA records (DNSSEC verified externally).

## RFCs in scope

- RFC 6698 — The DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol: TLSA
- RFC 7218 — Adding Acronyms to Simplify Conversations About DANE  
- RFC 7671 — The DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) Protocol: Updates and Operational Guidance
- RFC 7929 — DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) Bindings for OpenPGP (probably out of scope but cross-reference)
- RFC 8460 — SMTP TLS Reporting (related; out of scope here)

## Out of scope

- DNS resolution (in pkix-dane-resolver)
- SMTP-specific DANE policy (RFC 7672 — possibly a separate verify_smtp_dane helper later)
- Integration into pkix-chain (separate child)

## Acceptance

- [ ] no_std builds clean
- [ ] DaneError satisfies non-negotiable #6
- [ ] Four per-usage verify functions implemented
- [ ] Test fixtures: TLSA records + corresponding cert chains covering all four usages
- [ ] Differential oracle: at minimum, OpenSSL's danessl or sufficient public test vectors

## Stub status

{"design":"RESOLVER SEAM (decided 2026-11-24, Mark, interactive)

Follows Option C from PKIX-a1yc.10 (pkix-revocation-http/src/async_fetcher.rs:14-31), the workspace's settled async pattern:

- pkix-dane (no_std core) owns the SYNC seam only: TlsaResolver trait, DaneError, NoTlsaResolver zero-cost null impl, the TLSA record types, the matching functions, and TLSA owner-name construction (_443._tcp.host per RFC 6698 3, plus RFC 7671 7 CNAME/DNAME handling -- pure string work, no I/O, so it belongs here and NOT in the resolver crate as the current stub doc claims).
- pkix-dane-resolver (std) owns the ASYNC seam: AsyncTlsaResolver, behind an 'async' feature, plus hickory-backed reference impls of both. Async machinery must NOT appear in pkix-dane -- Option A was rejected for propagating async-trait / Send bounds into no_std consumers.
- No block_on bridge anywhere. Option B was rejected: 'Calling block_on from inside a running async runtime is a well-known footgun (deadlocks the executor).'
- Mechanism: async-trait macro, matching pkix-revocation-http. Native AFIT is now available (MSRV 1.87) but the switch is workspace-wide under PKIX-5hoi, not forked per-crate in a new crate.

RESOLVER RETURN TYPE

resolve() must NOT return a bare Vec<TlsaRecord>. DNSSEC state is security-critical and PKIX-j32w.4's failure-mode decision is made on it. Four distinct outcomes: secure-with-records (apply DANE), secure NODATA (authenticated denial, DANE deliberately absent), insecure/indeterminate (no DANE, fall through to PKIX), bogus (hard fail per RFC 7671). Return TlsaResponse { records, dnssec: DnssecStatus }. Precedent: pkix-revocation::OutOfScopeReason exists because the workspace already refuses to flatten 'the source did not cover this' into a bool. Per non-negotiable #6 the type needs Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq, Send + Sync, serde behind a flag -- which also rules out handing back a borrowed hickory type.

DER EXACTNESS -- CHANGES THE FILED SIGNATURES

The signatures in this bead's description (verify_pkix_ee(leaf: &Certificate, ...), verify_dane_ee(leaf: &Certificate, ...), verify_dane_ta(leaf: &Certificate, ...)) are WRONG as filed and must take the as-received DER.

TLSA selector 0 (Cert) with matching type 1/2 hashes the full certificate DER -- TBS + signatureAlgorithm + signatureValue -- exactly as the TLSA publisher computed it from their certificate file. x509-cert 0.3 made Certificate/TBSCertificate fields private AND normalizes validity times on re-encode (dates before 2050 become UTCTime), so cert.to_der() is not guaranteed to reproduce the bytes the peer presented. pkix-path/src/lib.rs:3104-3121 documents this for the signature case and ships tbs_certificate_der() as the workaround -- but that covers only the TBS portion. There is NO full-Certificate equivalent, and DANE needs the full cert.

A certificate whose issuer used GeneralizedTime for a pre-2050 validity date would therefore produce a hash that does not match its published TLSA record -- a silent interop failure against exactly the kind of CA that triggered the PKITS 4.2.4 / 4.2.7 regressions in commit 5a3ed995.

Rule: hash the bytes as received, never a re-encode. Selector 1 (SPKI) is less exposed since SPKI carries no time fields, but the uniform rule is safer and costs nothing -- TLS hands you the wire bytes anyway.

Shape: take the DER (and parse internally), or a PresentedCert<'a> { der: &'a [u8], parsed: &'a Certificate } pair. pkix-zlint-bridge::run_on_cert(cert_der: &[u8]) is the existing precedent for an entry point that needs exact bytes; no pattern yet exists for carrying as-received DER alongside a parsed cert, so this crate establishes it.

Matching type 0 (exact content match, no hash) has the same requirement for the same reason.

DEPENDENCY DIRECTION

verify_dane_ta returns a TrustAnchor and verify_pkix_ta takes &ValidatedPath, so pkix-dane depends on pkix-path + x509-cert. chain -> dane -> path, parallel to chain -> revocation -> path. Both no_std, so non-negotiable #1 is unaffected, but pkix-dane will not be dependency-free the way pkix-aia is.

STILL OPEN, DOES NOT BLOCK THIS BEAD

PKIX-j32w.3's feature-gate question (default-on dane vs split dane / dane-resolver). The trait shape is identical either way."}

{"notes":"PROGRESS 2026-11-24 — first increment landed (uncommitted).

SHIPPED
- pkix-dane/Cargo.toml: deps (x509-cert, der, sha2, optional serde), features std / serde, [[test]] round_trip gated on serde+std.
- src/record.rs — TlsaUsage / TlsaSelector / TlsaMatchingType as total enums over all 256 octet values (Unassigned(u8) + PrivateUse), TlsaRecord with from_rdata / to_rdata / is_usable.
- src/selector.rs — PresentedCert (received DER + parsed cert), selected_content, matches(), matching_records().
- src/name.rs — TlsaProtocol, TlsaName (_<port>._<proto>.<host>), DNS label/length validation.
- src/verify.rs — verify_dane_ee, verify_pkix_ee.
- src/lib.rs — DaneError (12 variants, hand-rolled Display per repo convention, no thiserror), DnssecStatus (Secure/Insecure/Indeterminate/Bogus + is_secure / permits_pkix_fallback), TlsaResponse (records + status, is_authenticated_denial, has_usable_record), TlsaResolver trait + batch_resolve default, NoTlsaResolver, non-negotiable #6 compile-time assertions.
- tests/ — 43 integration tests + 2 doc tests. Fixtures generated by tests/fixtures/gen.sh; expected digests come from openssl dgst, NOT from this crate's sha2, so the tests are differential rather than self-consistent.

GATES: fmt / clippy --all-targets --all-features / rustdoc -D warnings / typos all clean; tests green under all four feature combos (default, std, serde, std+serde).

NEW FINDING — verify_pkix_ta's filed signature is unimplementable
This bead's description specifies verify_pkix_ta(path: &ValidatedPath, tlsa: &[TlsaRecord]). pkix_path::ValidatedPath does not carry the chain certificates. Its fields are anchor_index, depth, leaf_subject, leaf_issuer, leaf_serial, leaf_spki, valid_policy_tree (verified by reading pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1277-1420). PKIX-TA (usage 0) must match a TLSA record against a trust anchor or intermediate in the validated chain, and none of those certificates is reachable from a ValidatedPath. anchor_index indexes into the caller's own anchors slice, so the certificates stay with the caller.

Corrected shape: verify_pkix_ta must take the chain (as PresentedCert values) and/or the anchor certificate, with the caller having separately established that PKIX path validation succeeded. This is the second signature error in the filed description, after the &Certificate / as-received-DER correction recorded in the design field.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD
1. verify_dane_ta — synthesize a TrustAnchor. Two sources: a cert in the peer's presented chain that matches a DANE-TA record, or, for selector Cert + matching type Full, the anchor certificate carried in the record's association data itself. pkix_path::TrustAnchor::from_cert(Certificate) exists and takes ownership, so synthesis is straightforward. Return the anchor plus which source it came from — the distinction is operationally meaningful. Re-adds the pkix-path dependency (currently commented out of Cargo.toml with that reason).
2. verify_pkix_ta — per the corrected signature above.
3. GeneralizedTime regression test. The DER-exactness design is currently justified by reasoning plus an SPKI-vs-openssl check (tests/matching.rs::spki_selector_reproduces_openssl_spki_der), but there is NO test with a certificate that actually carries a pre-2050 GeneralizedTime validity date — the input that would break a to_der()-based implementation. Building one needs hand-assembled DER, since openssl emits UTCTime there. Worth doing: it is the only test that would catch a regression back to re-encoding. DANE matching never checks signatures, so the fixture does not need a valid signature.
4. no_std bare-metal verification. Source-level no_std IS verified (building with default features puts #![no_std] in force; a probe referencing std:: fails to compile, and the same probe compiles with --features std). NOT verified: that the dependency tree builds for a bare-metal target. rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabi failed in this environment. pkix-path already builds for riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf and thumbv7em-none-eabi with the same der / x509-cert / sha2 pins, so this is expected to pass, but it is unconfirmed.
5. Version bump. The crate is published at 0.1.0 as a stub; substantive content needs 0.2.0 plus the workspace Cargo.toml path-dep pin and a CHANGELOG entry. Left alone deliberately — that is a release step, not part of this bead."}

resolve() must NOT return a bare Vec<TlsaRecord>. DNSSEC state is security-critical and PKIX-j32w.4's failure-mode decision is made on it. Four distinct outcomes: secure-with-records (apply DANE), secure NODATA (authenticated denial, DANE deliberately absent), insecure/indeterminate (no DANE, fall through to PKIX), bogus (hard fail per RFC 7671). Return TlsaResponse { records, dnssec: DnssecStatus }. Precedent: pkix-revocation::OutOfScopeReason exists because the workspace already refuses to flatten 'the source did not cover this' into a bool. Per non-negotiable #6 the type needs Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq, Send + Sync, serde behind a flag -- which also rules out handing back a borrowed hickory type.

DER EXACTNESS -- CHANGES THE FILED SIGNATURES

The signatures in this bead's description (verify_pkix_ee(leaf: &Certificate, ...), verify_dane_ee(leaf: &Certificate, ...), verify_dane_ta(leaf: &Certificate, ...)) are WRONG as filed and must take the as-received DER.

TLSA selector 0 (Cert) with matching type 1/2 hashes the full certificate DER -- TBS + signatureAlgorithm + signatureValue -- exactly as the TLSA publisher computed it from their certificate file. x509-cert 0.3 made Certificate/TBSCertificate fields private AND normalizes validity times on re-encode (dates before 2050 become UTCTime), so cert.to_der() is not guaranteed to reproduce the bytes the peer presented. pkix-path/src/lib.rs:3104-3121 documents this for the signature case and ships tbs_certificate_der() as the workaround -- but that covers only the TBS portion. There is NO full-Certificate equivalent, and DANE needs the full cert.

A certificate whose issuer used GeneralizedTime for a pre-2050 validity date would therefore produce a hash that does not match its published TLSA record -- a silent interop failure against exactly the kind of CA that triggered the PKITS 4.2.4 / 4.2.7 regressions in commit 5a3ed995.

Rule: hash the bytes as received, never a re-encode. Selector 1 (SPKI) is less exposed since SPKI carries no time fields, but the uniform rule is safer and costs nothing -- TLS hands you the wire bytes anyway.

Shape: take the DER (and parse internally), or a PresentedCert<'a> { der: &'a [u8], parsed: &'a Certificate } pair. pkix-zlint-bridge::run_on_cert(cert_der: &[u8]) is the existing precedent for an entry point that needs exact bytes; no pattern yet exists for carrying as-received DER alongside a parsed cert, so this crate establishes it.

Matching type 0 (exact content match, no hash) has the same requirement for the same reason.

DEPENDENCY DIRECTION

verify_dane_ta returns a TrustAnchor and verify_pkix_ta takes &ValidatedPath, so pkix-dane depends on pkix-path + x509-cert. chain -> dane -> path, parallel to chain -> revocation -> path. Both no_std, so non-negotiable #1 is unaffected, but pkix-dane will not be dependency-free the way pkix-aia is.

STILL OPEN, DOES NOT BLOCK THIS BEAD
